items.title: Chuck Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 7, 2023
items.q: It was from the first time we played, we both recognized that

ctx.x: And that was happening I think, and he would do something and almost instantaneously you played in a fashion that enhanced or went with it. And vice versa when you started playing.

Yeah he’s a cat that — that connection is very deep like that. It was from the first time we played, we both recognized that, I mean culturally very different upbringings but the improv thing, the freedom improv thing just jelled with us.

There was a part in the middle of it where I suggest people get on the Internet and try to find it, where it was like you turned into J.S. Bach for a little while. It was sort of a contrapuntal two thing. But going back to the wrong note business, and I wish I could think of a better term than wrong — unintended perhaps. If you’re playing with other people, bass and guitar especially, and they’re playing the changes, do you play differently than if you were playing the same song but by yourself?
